## Function Parse Turn

One model turn of the scout protocol read as one action (the lines not run named), one final answer (with or without the verb) or a malformed turn with its reason.

Behaviour: parseTurn(text: string | null) → Turn. VERBS = ["READ", "GREP", "LIST", "ANSWER"]. 1. null, or a text whose trim is "" → malformed "empty turn". 2. lines = text split on "\n", one trailing "\r" removed from each; an action line is a line whose trimStart matches /^(READ|GREP|LIST|ANSWER)(?=\s|$)/ (upper case only; prose and fence lines around it are ignored). 3. Some action line is an ANSWER line → the answer of the first one (step 6); the other action lines are ignored. 4. No action line: the whole text read as step 6 reads rest gives a JSON object with the key "targets" → that answer, checked as in step 6 (a bare or fenced JSON answer); else malformed "no action: one line must start with READ, GREP, LIST or ANSWER". 5. Else the action lines, each trimmed, repeats dropped (the first of equal lines kept, in order): the first is the action, read below (a malformed first line → that malformed turn); the others are skipped: {kind "action", action, skipped: their lines} when there are any, no key skipped when there are none. args = the action line trimmed, without its verb, trimmed. READ: args "" → "READ needs a path"; args matching /^(.*\S)\s+(\d+)-(\d+)$/ → path = group 1, from and to = Number of groups 2 and 3, from < 1 or to < from → "READ: bad line range <from>-<to>"; else path = args, from and to null. GREP: split args at its LAST " -- ": pattern = the part before, trimmed, path = the part after, trimmed; without " -- " the pattern is args and the path "". A pattern matching /^\/(.+)\/[a-z]*$/ becomes its group 1 (a /…/ literal's slashes and flags dropped). pattern "" → "GREP needs a pattern"; new RegExp(pattern) throws → "GREP: invalid pattern /<pattern>/". LIST: path = args ("" is the root). 6. ANSWER: rest = the ANSWER line (trimStart) after its verb, then every following line, "\n"-joined. From rest's first "{": the text up to the "}" that closes it, braces counted outside JSON strings (a string runs from a '"' to the next '"' not escaped by "\"); when none closes it or that text does not parse, the text up to rest's last "}". No "{", or no "}" after it → "ANSWER: no JSON object"; neither text parses → "ANSWER: the JSON does not parse"; not an object, or targets not an array of non-empty strings with at least one → "ANSWER: targets must be a non-empty list of paths"; context_slice absent → [], else an array of non-empty strings ("ANSWER: context_slice must be a list of paths"); reasoning absent → "", else a string ("ANSWER: reasoning must be a string"); the answer carries only targets, context_slice, reasoning, in that order, the lists as given. Results: {kind "action", action: {kind "read", path, from, to} | {kind "grep", pattern, path} | {kind "list", path}, skipped?}, {kind "answer", answer}, {kind "malformed", reason}; keys in these orders.

## Function Run Tool

One READ, GREP or LIST executed over the listing through the cage and the injected file system, its text capped in lines and characters; LIST shows each file's line count.

Behaviour: runTool(action, tree, fs, caps {readLines, readChars?, grepHits, grepLineChars, listEntries, grepSkip: string[]}) → {text, read: action is a READ, error: string | null}. DEFAULT_TOOL_CAPS = {readLines 400, readChars 12000, grepHits 200, grepLineChars 300, listEntries 300, grepSkip [".morph", "decks"]}. A failure: error = its message, text = "<READ|GREP|LIST> failed: <error>"; else error null and text = its lines "\n"-joined, no final newline. A file's lines: its text split on "\n", one trailing "\r" removed from each, the last piece dropped when it is "". The listing is walked in code-unit order. READ: Cage Path (file) refused → its error; fs.readFile(posix join of root and the caged path) throws → "unreadable: <path>"; a "\0" in it → "binary file: <path>"; 0 lines → the one line "READ <path>: empty file"; from = action.from ?? 1, from > n lines → "line range <from>-<action.to ?? n> is past the end (<n> lines): <path>"; to = min(action.to ?? n, n), last = min(to, from + readLines − 1); when caps.readChars is set, the shown lines "<i>: <line i>" from `from` on are kept while the sum of their lengths, each + 1, stays ≤ readChars, at least one, and last = the last kept (a first shown line longer than readChars is its first readChars chars + "… (+<the rest's length> chars)"): "READ <path> lines <from>-<last> of <n>", then the shown lines, then when last < to "… <to − last> more lines; READ <path> <last + 1>-<to> for the next". GREP: new RegExp(pattern) (no flags) throws → "invalid pattern /<pattern>/"; Cage Path (dir) refused → its error; skip = grepSkip, or none when the caged path's first segment is in grepSkip; each listed file under the caged path whose first segment is not skipped: Cage Path (file) refused or readFile throws → counted refused; a "\0" → passed over silently; each line i that the pattern tests true is a match, shown while fewer than grepHits are shown as "<file>:<i>: <line>", a line longer than grepLineChars as its first grepLineChars chars + "… (+<the rest's length> chars)". Lines: "GREP /<pattern>/ in <'the tree' or the caged path + '/'>: <m> match|matches in <f> file|files" (f = files with a match), the shown matches, "… <m − shown> more matches" when any left, "(<r> file|files refused by the cage)" when r > 0. LIST: Cage Path (dir) refused → its error; entries = the next segment of each listed file under the caged path: a file name, or a directory name + "/" with the count of its files; entries in code-unit order: "LIST <'.' or the caged path + '/'>: <k> entry|entries", the first listEntries as "<dir>/ (<c> file|files)" or, for a file, "<name> (<n> line|lines)" with n its lines read through Cage Path (file) and fs.readFile of its listed path, "<name> (binary)" for a "\0", the name alone when refused or unreadable; "… <k − listEntries> more entries" when more. LIST and GREP never read a directory; LIST reads only the files it shows.
